findings.explanation: The core comparison named in the title is left undefined. No sunset or twilight lookup is named, no site-to-camera mapping or latitude/longitude field is listed, and the SPL never joins against one, so a reader cannot build the comparison.
findings.suggested_fix: Name the lookup (for example a per-site, per-date sunrise/sunset CSV with `site`, `date`, `sunset_epoch`, `sunrise_epoch`) and how it is produced (for example an NOAA solar calculator export). List the `camera_id`→`site` mapping, and give the comparison (activation time minus sunset, flagged beyond N minutes).

findings.explanation: The data sources do not name the fields the SPL needs (`mode`, `camera_id`) or the vendor event that reports a day/night or IR-cut filter change. Sibling UCs use `cctv:analytics` for people counting and ANPR, not device day/night state, so the sourcetype choice is unexplained.
findings.quote: `index=physical` · `sourcetype="cctv:analytics"` Collected via Universal Forwarder (Splunkbase 617) modular input or scripted poll
findings.suggested_fix: Name the source event, for example the ONVIF imaging or IR-cut state change, or the Hikvision ISAPI day/night switch setting. List the extracted fields (`camera_id`, `mode`, camera `site`), or move the feed to the device-diagnostic sourcetype the siblings use for camera state.

findings.explanation: The UC is marked verified by `catalog-team`, but its description, false positives, evidence, exclusions and detailed implementation are template text, and its title's sunset comparison is not implemented. That does not reflect SME sign-off.
findings.suggested_fix: Change the status to draft or unverified until an SME has reviewed a working sunset-comparison implementation.

findings.explanation: None of the listed causes would make a camera switch to IR early or late. The obvious data-center case is missing: indoor cameras switch on room lighting, not sunset, so the sunset comparison is meaningless for them.
findings.quote: Synthetic probe on `camera_id`, `hour`** — Health checks in `physical` populate the same fields the SPL groups on.
findings.suggested_fix: List real causes: indoor hall or cage cameras where IR follows the light schedule; overcast or storm conditions triggering early IR; floodlights or vehicle headlights delaying or reversing IR; cameras set to a fixed schedule rather than auto light-sensor mode; and hysteresis that makes a camera flap between modes at dusk. Exclude indoor cameras by lookup.

findings.explanation: The steps are a generic skeleton that disagrees with this UC. The SPL hard-codes `earliest=-7d`; "route critical severity to the platform on-call" contradicts `criticality: low`; and a 7-day hourly heatmap is a report, not a paging alert. There is no step covering the sunset lookup or the timezone.
findings.quote: Schedule the SPL with earliest=-24h@h and throttle per entity to avoid duplicate pages.
findings.suggested_fix: Rewrite the steps as a weekly report: ingest mode-change events, build and maintain the sunset lookup, convert `_time` to site-local time, compute the activation offset from sunset per camera and day, and review outliers. Drop the paging and throttling text.

findings.explanation: The Search Reference landing page URL has no apostrophe. The canonical path is `.../SearchReference/WhatsInThisManual`.
findings.suggested_fix: Use https://docs.splunk.com/Documentation/Splunk/latest/SearchReference/WhatsInThisManual and add a reference for the sunrise/sunset data source.

findings.explanation: The heatmap shows when IR is active but not how far activation is from sunset, which is the stated point of the UC.
findings.suggested_fix: Add a per-camera chart or table of the activation offset from sunset (minutes) over time, with the heatmap as context.

firewalled_field_flags.issue: The title promises a comparison against the local sunset window, but the SPL never references sunset, site location or local time. Either the SPL must add a sunset lookup join or the title should be narrowed to "CCTV IR Night Mode Activation by Hour".

`strftime(_time,"%H")` renders the hour in the search user's timezone, not the camera site's local time, so hourly buckets are skewed for multi-timezone estates. The regex `ir|night|mono` also matches any mode string containing "ir" (for example IR-cut filter state values), so the mode literals should be anchored.

summary: The UC promises to compare infrared night-mode activation with each site's local sunset, but nothing in the text or the SPL provides sunset data, site location or timezone handling. The search only counts night-mode events per camera per hour. Nearly every prose field is template text, yet the UC is marked `verified`.
